criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear rationale and users (marine/conservation scientists, reef managers implied) with footnoted sources. However, mission goals, objectives and requirements are not formally specified, the satellite's payload and specific function are vague, and the 'Oceans 30% more acidic' claim is loosely tied to bleaching. Users are identified but not fully developed.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with task descriptions, deadlines and reserved editing week provides some contingency. Planned sources and STK simulation sequencing are shown. Contingency and variations are limited, and linkage to mission narrative is modest, so placed at the lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is described only as tutorials and reading. No preliminary orbit, launch or STK results, figures or interpretation are presented, so the technical evidence is insufficient for on-track status.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and reasonable structure with footnoted references. Some inconsistencies: the 'Completed stages are gold' colour description and figure reference are informal; the 'more acidic' claim is inaccurately phrased (pH decrease); the ASU Asner reference is a citation placeholder; a stray apostrophe-level grammar issue appears. Figure is labelled but caption absent.

evidence.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution
Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue.

technical_issues.issue: Claim that oceans are '30 percent more acidic' is incorrect phrasing; acidity increase corresponds to ~30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration (pH drop ~0.1).
Bathymetry resolution statement (100 m per pixel) is not a meaningful comparison to mission sensor requirements and no orbit/sensor requirements are derived.
Software selection (STK) is mentioned only via tutorials; no justification or statement of licence/approval given.
No orbit altitude, inclination, launch site or space-segment analysis presented, so R2 not addressed.

overall: Good rationale and a detailed Gantt chart, but the report lacks mission requirements, space-segment analysis, and substantive preliminary technical results. Software choice and some factual phrasing need tightening. Overall a satisfactory but incomplete Part 1 submission.

feedback.summary: You have a clear rationale for monitoring the Great Barrier Reef and a detailed Gantt chart with a reserved review week, which together make a solid Part 1 base. The report would be stronger with formal mission requirements, a space-segment analysis (orbit, inclination, launch site), and actual preliminary STK results. Please also correct the acidity statement and justify your software choice.
next_steps: Add a short requirements table in Mission Concept & Rationale, linking each goal and user need to a measurable requirement such as revisit time, spatial resolution or latency.
Present a space-segment analysis in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, including orbit altitude, inclination and launch site, with a brief note on why each was chosen.
Show at least one STK output (such as an orbit or ground-track figure) with a caption and a sentence interpreting what it means for your mission.

criteria.C1: Your rationale clearly explains why reef monitoring matters and identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, with footnoted sources. To reach the next level, state formal mission goals, objectives and requirements, and show how the satellite's payload and function meet specific user needs. Also correct the '30 percent more acidic' claim in Mission Concept & Rationale; the change is in hydrogen ion concentration, corresponding to a pH drop of about 0.1. The 100 m per pixel bathymetry figure needs to be linked to sensor requirements.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart includes task descriptions, deadlines and a reserved review week in Week 10, which gives useful contingency and makes the plan feasible. Planned information sources are shown. To strengthen it, explain more clearly how the plan follows from the mission concept, and add further contingencies for variations, such as delays in STK simulation or data access.
criteria.C3: You have completed STK tutorials 1 to 4 and read background material, which shows you have started. However, no orbit, launch or simulation results are presented, so there is little evidence of technical progress. Include at least one preliminary result with a brief interpretation to show you are on track for completion.
criteria.C4: The report uses clear headings and a logical structure, and references are footnoted. To reach the next level, use more formal language instead of phrases such as 'Completed stages are gold', correct the pH wording, and make the Asner reference a complete citation rather than a placeholder. Add a caption to your figure so readers can follow it without the surrounding text.
